text:
Vegas arrives on the second night of a back-to-back, having lost 3-2 in a shootout at Boston last night. The Golden Knights are 1-2-2 in their last five and without Parker Wotherspoon. Pittsburgh has had two days off since a 5-4 loss at Montreal, whose five straight wins made it a tough one. The Penguins are missing Bryan Rust (lower body), and Tommy Novak, who plays his 300th NHL game tonight, has taken his spot beside Crosby and Rakell, up to 17:47 a night from 14:05. Vegas won the first meeting 6-2 on Oct. 17, a game we figured they deserved 34% of the time by chance quality, so that result may have flattered Pittsburgh's opponent less than the score suggests.

At five on five the teams are close in expected goals, meaning the quality of chances: Vegas has taken 54% of them and Pittsburgh 52%. Vegas allows fewer per 60 (2.64 to 3.44), and its power play (0.70 expected goals a game) is well ahead of Pittsburgh's (0.45). Our model has it 3.22 to 3.08 for Vegas. In net, projected starters Adin Hill (-2.4 goals saved above expected, a measure of saves beyond what shot quality predicts) and Arturs Silovs (+2.3) are both at .89 save percentages, though Silovs has the better numbers this year.

Watch Mitch Marner, on a 10-game point streak (1 goal, 14 assists) and 73% for a point. Jack Eichel is 74% for a point, and Mark Stone has our top goal chance for Vegas at 37%. For Pittsburgh, Sidney Crosby is 31% to score, with Rickard Rakell at 30%. Our under-the-radar picks: Vegas's Tomas Hertl, who has 3.0 expected goals in his last 10 games on third-line minutes, and Pittsburgh's Ben Kindel, 46% for a point after moving into the top six.
